summary.intent: Continue ongoing work on the Caliper project docs: reframe how recall against RDT is presented so it doesn't read as a correctness measure.
summary.outcome: Inspected origin/main docs (rdt-differences.md, measurement.md) and launched a docs worker on branch `docs/rdt-recall-framing` to edit the README, docs/measurement.md, docs/STATUS.md and the weekly record. It is to define recall, put checker-judged wrong-rate figures beside it from the existing 2026-11-06 table, and use no new numbers. A parallel S6 (watch mode) task was also running; neither had finished at the end of the transcript.

repo: Recall-against-RDT framing appears in several places: README, docs/measurement.md, docs/STATUS.md, and possibly the weekly record text.
The 2026-11-06 table already holds checker-judged figures, e.g. spectrum: Caliper wrong 1.09% vs RDT wrong 5.02% on listed props, which can be cited without recomputation.
docs/rdt-differences.md and docs/measurement.md on origin/main were inspected with git show, and measurement.md was grepped for headings and 'recall'.
workflow: Use `git show origin/main:<path>` with sed/grep/cut to inspect docs on main without switching branches.
Delegating doc edits to a worker agent on a dedicated branch lets work run in parallel with other tasks such as S6 watch mode.
When a request is ambiguous (the 'chart'), state the assumption and have the worker report what it shows and propose a replacement rather than regenerating it.
